avoid_supplements.name: Calcium supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Fosfomycin forms insoluble chelate complexes with divalent cations (calcium, magnesium, iron), significantly reducing bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Separate administration by at least 2-3 hours; take fosfomycin on empty stomach

avoid_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Divalent cation binding reduces fosfomycin absorption and urinary concentration needed for UTI efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Separate dosing by 2-3 hours minimum; avoid concurrent intake

avoid_supplements.name: Iron supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Iron (ferrous/ferric) chelation with fosfomycin impairs drug absorption and bioavailability
avoid_supplements.action: Take fosfomycin 2-3 hours apart from iron; preferably on empty stomach

caution_supplements.name: Zinc supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential minor chelation with fosfomycin; clinical significance unclear but theoretical interaction exists
caution_supplements.action: Monitor therapeutic response; space dosing if possible

avoid_foods.name: Dairy products (milk, cheese, yogurt)
avoid_foods.mechanism: High calcium content chelates fosfomycin, reducing absorption by 30-50% and lowering urinary drug levels required for bactericidal activity
avoid_foods.action: Avoid dairy within 2 hours before and after fosfomycin dose; take on empty stomach

avoid_foods.name: Fortified cereals and grain products
avoid_foods.mechanism: Added iron and calcium fortification can reduce fosfomycin bioavailability
avoid_foods.action: Separate consumption by at least 2 hours from fosfomycin dose

caution_foods.name: High-fiber foods
caution_foods.mechanism: May reduce fosfomycin absorption rate; minimal clinical impact but theoretically relevant
caution_foods.action: Consistency in timing with fosfomycin dosing is preferred

monitoring_notes: Fosfomycin should be taken on an empty stomach with water to maximize absorption and achieve adequate urinary concentrations. Monitor for adequate therapeutic response and counsel patients to strictly avoid concurrent divalent cation supplements and dairy products, particularly for single-dose UTI treatment where absorption is critical.
